solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ahead of time, borders of magnolia escape disease that's spotted in gardens

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the second
the border letters escape from the illness word, so they drop out of it

parts.note: a malady is a disease

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: bird is slang for time served in prison

explanation.surface: A gardener worries that a disease is getting out among the magnolias ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: MA, the borders of 'magnolia', escape from MALADY to leave LADY, which goes 'Ahead of' BIRD, British slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The beetle with spotted wing cases is a familiar insect on garden plants, where it eats aphids.

clue.text: Fifty selfies oddly lacking any vitality

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the letters of the word selfies are arranged in an odd, strange way

explanation.surface: A dull set of fifty phone self-portraits with no energy in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like it wants alternate letters, but here it means strangely, a rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no vitality at all is dead or inert, synonyms for this adjective.

clue.text: Adding sixty after subtracting every other number

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction: add sixty once you have taken away every other number.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection runs across both words, keeping the second, fourth and so on; 'after' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral, and in a broader sense any number from nought to nine.

clue.text: Composer and famous songwriter shortly going to Australia

indicators.note: shortly means the songwriter's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Irving Berlin wrote White Christmas
Oz is an informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A composer and a celebrated songwriter will soon be heading to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The songwriter is Irving Berlin, writer of White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was the French Romantic composer of the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Female gets cut from straightforward foul

indicators.note: the female letter is removed from the front of the honest word

parts.note: frank means straightforward, candid

explanation.surface: A woman's blunt remarks are edited out for being offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling or offensive, as in a rank odour.

clue.text: Force of habit wearing uniform? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece wearing another sits inside it
this reverses the stated arrangement, so the uniform goes inside the habit rather than the other way round

parts.note: a habit is a form of dress, as worn by a nun
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A habit forced on someone, like wearing a uniform, is turned on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit wearing uniform' would put DRESS inside U; 'On the contrary' flips it so U goes inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion or coercion, threats that force someone to act.

clue.text: Very many met up as arranged, having space

indicators.note: the letters of met up are arranged into a new order

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Lots of people gathered as planned, with room to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: METUP is rearranged to UMPTE, then EN, a printer's space, is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Comfortable place to relax, say, I reach when tipsy

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady from drink, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone a little drunk heads for the comfy chair to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholstered armchair is a classic comfortable seat for unwinding.

clue.text: Nick runs after player achieving a touchdown?

indicators.note: the runs letter comes after the nick word

parts.note: to score is to nick or scratch a mark
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A player named Nick runs in after a try in rugby or American football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is a verb meaning to scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchdown puts points on the board, so the player making it is one who scores, with the question mark showing it is one example.

clue.text: Prices broken by hollow iron statuettes

indicators.note: the price word is split open and the other piece put inside

parts.note: figures are prices or sums quoted

indicators.note: hollow means with the inside removed, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: The cost of figures cast in hollow iron gets broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow iron' leaves IN, which breaks into FIGURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurines are small ornamental statues, typically of china or metal.

clue.text: Irish aboard train causing trouble

indicators.note: the Irish abbreviation goes on board, inside the train word

parts.note: a string is a train or series of things

explanation.surface: An Irish passenger on a train is making mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring as an adjective means provoking trouble, as in stirring things up.

clue.text: Sauce of political journalist to ignore leader of Nationalists

indicators.note: the leading letter of the nationalists is ignored, so dropped from the name

parts.note: Robert Peston is a British political journalist on ITV

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political journalist's cheek in snubbing the head of the Nationalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks like cheek; it is the definition in its food sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and Parmesan.

clue.text: Energy during line dance to express oneself without restraint

indicators.note: the energy letter comes during, inside, the line and dance pair

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Line dancing gives someone the energy to cut loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Let rip is an idiom for acting or speaking freely without holding back.

clue.text: Main Conservative interrupts Telegraph smart alec

indicators.note: the pieces break into the telegraph word

parts.note: a wire is a telegram or telegraph message
the main is the sea

explanation.surface: A leading Tory butts in at the Telegraph newspaper, being a know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' looks like the newspaper this puzzle appears in; it is WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who pretends to know everything, a know-all.

clue.text: Ace under pressure to stop upset exhausts Nadal perhaps

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these letters go inside
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: drains means exhausts or uses up

indicators.note: in a down clue the ace letter sits under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A tennis ace under pressure tires out Nadal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DRAINS into SNIARD, and PA goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafael Nadal is from Spain, so he is an example of someone from that country.

clue.text: Worried Azeri on ship hugs child exhibiting illness

indicators.note: the anagram wraps around the child abbreviation
worried means agitated, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: An anxious man from Azerbaijan on board ship holds a sick child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' turns AZERIONSHIP into SIZOPHRENIA, which 'hugs' CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Schizophrenia is a serious mental disorder affecting thought and perception.

clue.text: Surprised expression over small number originally making annual celebration

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: hallo is an exclamation of surprise
wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A surprised cry greets a small figure at the start of a yearly festivity.
explanation.definitionFit: The eve of All Saints' Day on 31 October is celebrated every year with costumes.

clue.text: Brings food to table in French porcelain?

parts.note: Sevres porcelain is made in France; the clue's answer, written upwards in a down light, would spell that porcelain

explanation.surface: Dinner is presented on fine French china.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: SERVES written up the grid reads SEVRES, the French porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out food at the table is to present a meal to diners.

clue.text: Liberal making bow, it shows progress in education

parts.note: earning means making money
a bow is a curve

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician bows out, a sign of educational progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph of acquired skill over time plots how fast someone picks up a subject.

clue.text: Old general's command essentially beginning to end, maybe

parts.note: Mark Antony was a Roman general

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient general issues an order from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the seven-letter 'command' is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginning and end are opposites, so one is an example of a word of opposite meaning to the other.

clue.text: Firm is defending clumsy window cleaner

indicators.note: the firm and is pieces defend the clumsy word by surrounding it

parts.note: Co is an abbreviation for company, a firm
ham means clumsy or inexpert, as in ham-fisted

explanation.surface: A company protects an awkward worker who washes windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm is' reads as a phrase, but both words are pieces that wrap round the clumsy word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather cloth used to polish glass is named after a goat-like mountain antelope.

clue.text: Bill needs Guy to provide agreement

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a guy is a rope or cord that steadies a tent

explanation.surface: Bill and Guy need to reach a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Guy' look like names; a guy is a tent rope.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal agreement or treaty between parties.

clue.text: European native bird, one from the East, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a crow is a bird and an Asian is someone from the East

explanation.surface: A local bird, or perhaps one from Asia, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native bird' wants to be one piece, but 'native' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Croatia is a native of that Balkan country in Europe.

clue.text: Advanced technology initially installed in revolutionary commercial vehicles?

definitions.text: Advanced technology initially installed in revolutionary commercial vehicles?

indicators.note: the initials are put inside the reversed vehicle word
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: vans are commercial vehicles

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: High-tech gadgetry fitted in groundbreaking delivery vans.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: such systems are typically fitted in vans.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellite navigation is advanced technology commonly fitted in vans and lorries.

clue.text: Sky News to be positioned outside Scottish town

indicators.note: the news letters sit outside the sky word

parts.note: N is short for new, so news gives two of them
the air is the sky

explanation.surface: A satellite news channel sets up in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky News' looks like the TV channel; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a seaside town on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Shock description of cafe from those withholding tips

indicators.note: tips are the end letters of each word, held back so only the middle ones remain

explanation.surface: A cafe is shocked by customers who refuse to leave a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like surprise; it means a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick bushy mass, and this hairstyle is one.

clue.text: Good few periodically working in concert hall

indicators.note: periodically picks letters at regular intervals, every second one

parts.note: on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A decent handful perform now and then in a concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon comes from the ancient Greek building for musical performances.

clue.text: Retired neighbours' lid off a dustbin covers up flowers

indicators.note: Retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase covers up the letters, which sit concealed across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retired neighbour takes the lid off a bin and finds blooms underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'covers up flowers' as the definition, but 'covers up' is the concealment indicator, so the definition is just 'flowers'; 'Retired' reads the concealed letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow trumpet-shaped spring blooms of the narcissus family.

clue.text: Busy Monday for energetic individual

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A hectic start to the week suits a go-getter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a lively, forceful person, from the generator.

clue.text: See, one's awfully excited to exercise

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: up means excited, as in being worked up

explanation.surface: Someone is wildly thrilled at the prospect of a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully excited' looks like one phrase, but 'awfully' acts on ONES to give OSEN, and 'excited' is UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming up the muscles before exercise is limbering them, the verb sense here.
